title: Your face is glowing… but your life is hiding something.
paragraphs: Your face is glowing… but your life is hiding something.

Because it’s possible to look like Moses…
and live like the crowd around the golden calf.

You can carry the tablets…
and still carry secret sin.

You can speak “God is good”…
while your private life whispers something else.
What happens when glory touches a life that still has shadows?

Moses walks down the mountain after meeting God—
and his face is shining so intensely that people back away.

Light doesn’t negotiate with darkness.
It reveals it.
This moment comes right after one of Israel’s darkest failures.
They traded the living God for something they could control.
Here’s the truth that hits like thunder:
God is not impressed by reflected light that hides unrepented sin.
Listen to what God declares about Himself:
“The LORD, the LORD, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness…” — Exodus 34:6

God reveals His glory not just in power—
but in mercy.
Some scholars interpret this moment as the clearest self-revelation of God in the Old Testament—where His justice and mercy meet without contradiction.
And still chooses to make a way.
“The Israelites could not gaze at Moses’ face because of its glory, which was being brought to an end…” — 2 Corinthians 3:7

You can have moments with God…
and still fade back into old patterns.

You can cry at the altar…
and still return to the same chains.
This is where Jesus steps in—
But as the fulfillment Moses was pointing to.
“The Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we have seen His glory…” — John 1:14
Moses covered his face with a veil.
“And the curtain of the temple was torn in two…” — Matthew 27:51
“I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you…” — Ezekiel 36:26
You are not just someone who needs improvement.
You are someone who needs redemption.
And no amount of “glow” can cover that.
But Jesus didn’t come to expose you and leave you there.
Your hidden sin wasn’t hidden anymore.
“He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree…” — 1 Peter 2:24

From covering your sin…
to confessing it.

From performing light…
to becoming transformed by it.
“And we all, with unveiled face, beholding the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image…” — 2 Corinthians 3:18
Where are you still wearing a “veil”?
Where are you managing appearance instead of surrendering reality?

Where are you glowing…
but not growing?
God is not asking you to shine harder.
He’s calling you to come closer.
Because real transformation doesn’t come from trying.
You don’t have to clean yourself before coming to Him.
Whisper it if you have to:
Let Him into the places you’ve locked.
Because the same God who made Moses’ face shine…
is ready to transform your entire life.
